title: Covariates
text:
Potential covariates were identified by assessing a series of univariable linear models with EI as the outcome. Variables meeting the inclusion criteria of p < .25 were included in subsequent multivariable models as covariates.
Covariates identified and included in all subsequent models were gender, age, and several UTAUT variables including:

Performance expectancy
Hedonic motivation
Habit
Perceived Risk
Health Consciousness
Satisfaction

Results of the univariable linear models on selected covariates are shown in Table 1.

As shown in Table 2, The sample was predominantly female (67.3%), with a mean age of 15.4 years (SD = 1.4). The majority of participants were heterosexual (83.7%) and spoke English at home (95.4%). The mean EI score was 38.4% (SD = 18.7) and ranged between 0% and 78.1% (see Figure 2 for plot). Following Taki et al., the interquartile ranges were used for categorising engagement levels. Scores less than or equal to Q1 (28.7%) were indicative of poor engagement, scores between Q1 and Q3 (51.8%) were indicative of moderate engagement, and scores above Q3 were indicative of high engagement. Most participants were in the moderate engagement category (n = 131 ; 49.8 %), and there were no significant differences in demographic variables between engagement categories (Table 2). Figure 3 shows the trajectories for each of the sub-indices over the study period (note that Fi is not included as it was only measured at one time point).

title: The Triple E Project
text:
This project contains the analysis for the Triple E trial.
The published protocol can be viewed here @ BMC Public Health
The trial is registered at the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12623000399695). Date registered: 19/04/2023.

title: The Triple E Project
text:
Background
Digital, or eHealth, interventions are highly promising approaches to help adolescents improve their health behaviours and reduce their risk of chronic disease. However, they often have low uptake and retention. There is also a paucity of high-quality research into the predictors of eHealth engagement, and a lack of studies that have systematically evaluated existing engagement strategies in adolescent populations. This randomised controlled trial primarily aims to assess the effectiveness of different strategies in increasing engagement with a healthy lifestyles app, Health4Life. Associations between the engagement strategies and improvements in adolescent health behaviours (healthy eating, physical activity, sleep, recreational screen time, smoking, alcohol use) will also be examined, along with potential predictors of adolescents’ intentions to use health apps and their use of the Health4Life app.

title: The Triple E Project
text:
Methods
The trial uses a 2x2x2x2 full factorial design, with four engagement strategies (gamification, health coaching, parent resources, and text messages) as the factors. All participants received access to the Health4Life app. Participants were randomly allocated to one of 16 conditions (different combinations of the four engagement. strategies to be evaluated). Adolescents and parents/guardians completed baseline assessments and a follow-up assessment after 3 months. The primary outcome, app engagement, is assessed via an app Engagement Index (EI) using data collected from the back-end of the Health4Life app, as well as the Mobile App Rating Scale - User Version (UMars), which is measured during the follow-up survey.

title: Balance Checks
text:
Sample sizes were mostly balanced across the 16 conditions (ranging from 15-18 per condition). Sample sizes were also balanced by strategy level (effect coded off/no = -1; on/yes = +1):

Gamification: Off/No (-1) = 128 | On/Yes (+1) = 135
Health coaching: Off/No (-1) = 133 | On/Yes (+1) = 130
Parent Resources: Off/No (-1) = 131 | On/Yes (+1) = 132
Text Messages Off/No (-1) = 131 | On/Yes (+1) = 132

Table 1 displays the descriptive statistics of each covariate by strategy received. results of regressions of the covariates onto the strategies. There were no significant differences in any of the covariates in whether each strategy was received or not received.

tbl_covars_cont <- dt_most |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = any_of(strategy_vars), 
names_to = "factor", values_to = "level") |> 
  group_by(factor, level) |> 
  summarise(
    across(any_of(cont_covars), 
  list(
    mean = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .names = "{.col}__{.fn}"),
  n = n(),
  .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(factor, level, n), 
    names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
    names_sep = "__") |> 
  mutate(
    stat = paste0(round(mean, 2), " (", round(sd, 2), ")")
  ) |> 
  select(factor, level, variable, stat)

tbl_covars_cat <- dt_most |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(strategy_vars),
    names_to = "factor", 
    values_to = "level") |>
  count(factor, level, across(any_of(cat_covars)), name = "n_cat") |> 
  group_by(factor, level) |>
  mutate(
    pct = n_cat / sum(n_cat) * 100
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # keep one reference category per categorical covariate, e.g. gender == "Female"
  filter(gender == "Woman or female") |>
  mutate(variable = "Gender (Woman or female)",
         stat = paste0(n_cat, " (", round(pct, 1), "%)")
        ) |>
  select(factor, level, variable, stat)

# function to make a row for regression results 

make_row <- function(v, strategy, is_categorical) {
  var_to_use <- if (is_categorical) paste0(v, "_binary") else v
  
  if (is_categorical) {
    # logistic regression; covariate coded as binary factor 
    mod <- glm(dt_most[[var_to_use]] ~ dt_most[[strategy]], family = binomial)

  } else {
    mod <- lm(dt_most[[var_to_use]] ~ dt_most[[strategy]])
  }
  ci <- confint(mod)[2, ]
  tibble(
    beta = coef(mod)[2],
    ci = paste0(round(ci[1], 2), ", ", round(ci[2], 2)),
    p = fmt_p(summary(mod)$coefficients[2, 4])
  )
}

run_balance_row <- function(v, label, is_categorical) {
  bind_cols(
    tibble(variable = label), 
    purrr::map_dfc(strategy_vars, \(s) {
      make_row(v, s, is_categorical) |> 
        rename_with(~ paste0(strategy_prefixes[[s]], .))
    })
  )
}

text: The primary analysis used an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) framework, implemented as an adjusted linear regression model with the four strategy factors and baseline covariates entered as predictors of EI. Strategy variables were effect coded, with absent/off coded as -1 and present/on coded; where each main effect coefficient represents half the adjusted difference between present and absent levels, averaged across the other factors.

title: Multiphase Optimisation Strategy Full Factorial Analyses
text:
Main Analyses
For the primary EI analysis, three models were estimated. First, a full factorial model included the four strategy main effects, all possible two-way interactions, all possible three-way interactions, the four-way interaction, and the selected covariates (see Table 3). Terms deemed significant (p < .10) were provisionally screened-in in the reduced model, otherwise they were screened out of the reduced model. Second, terms were screened again in the reduced model, and all significant screened-in components (p < .10) were included in the parsimonius model. Regression coefficients are reported with 90% confidence intervals. Estimated marginal means were calculated from the parsimonius EI model to describe the retained interactions. Predicted values were calculated from the parsimonius model for all 16 factorial conditions. These predicted values represent adjusted EI estimates with all covariates held at their means.
Full Factorial Model
The full factorial model including all covariates, strategies, and all possible two-three-and-four way interactions
